name: P1: background worker fan-out has no back-pressure (check_projects ~267% CPU)
description:
**Residual P1 from task `8f8710cf` (CRITICAL: Backend unresponsive). Its P0 shipped and was verified live; this item was explicitly left as "remaining work is P1, not P0" and had no card of its own (created by PM, shift 2026-11-16 19:25).**

1. **Evidence** — closing summary of `8f8710cf`: "background worker fan-out at ~267% CPU (`check_projects` has no back-pressure)", listed as P1 #8.
2. **Why it matters** — the P0 work brought the request path down to API CPU 1.3% / event-loop lag 12ms / TTFT 7.4s, but a background fan-out pegging ~267% CPU will still degrade response time for the user under load; it is the last known cause of the original "client waits for the backend" symptom.
3. **Related, already ticketed (do not duplicate):** `e65e733e` — chat storage folder layout (14MB JSON per chat, full rewrite per tool event).

**Objective:** background project checks run with bounded concurrency so they can never saturate the CPU or starve the event loop.

**Steps:**
1. Reproduce/measure: show `check_projects` (and the rest of the fan-out) sustained CPU and how many projects it walks concurrently.
2. Add bounded concurrency (semaphore/queue) plus a minimum interval between sweeps; skip a sweep if the previous one is still running instead of stacking.
3. Re-measure CPU and event-loop lag under the same conditions used for the P0 verification.

**Acceptance:** a measured before/after of fan-out CPU and event-loop lag; sweeps never stack; a test covers the "skip if already running" rule.

**Not in scope:** chat storage (`e65e733e`) and the `pytest:api` image issue.
